newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Nestle says still backs U.S. gene-soya.
newsitem.headline: Nestle says still backs U.S. gene-soya.

text.p: Nestle, the world's biggest food and beverage company, said it would stick by a corporate-wide policy of using soy products from genetically modified U.S. beans despite a boycott by its German subsidiary.
Nestle said German unit Nestle Deutschland AG was reacting to special local conditions by foreswearing any derivatives from the new soy beans being harvested in the 1996/97 U.S. crop.
Nestle Deutschland said on October 25 it would not use products from the beans becuase of expected consumer opposition but added it believed the beans were safe.

Germany has been a centre of campaigning against the modified beans by Greenpeace and consumer groups, who say a possible risk to human health cannot be ruled out as soya is used in some 30,000 food products.
The beans have been genetically modified to resist a weed killer in a technology developed by U.S. chemical company Monsanto.
At Nestle world headquarters in Vevey, Switzerland, a spokesman said corporate policy remained that there was "no reason to treat the genetically modified soy beans differently than other beans."

"If a Nestle company believes it has enough stored supplies or supplies from other countries, then it is within its discretion to act accordingly, but that has no effect whatsoever on the general corporate approach," spokesman Hans Joerg Renk said about Nestle Deutschland. -- Zurich Newsroom, +41-1-631 7340
